# Three literal leaves — source-only alias/body amendment

HOLD_OPERATIONAL / HOLD_EXTERNAL. Original readers/receipts remain immutable.
New three_leaves.proposed.mjs.txt has a false source guard and no CLI or
automatic call. Filling REQUEST.disabled.json cannot enable it. A separately
reviewed one-constant enabled-source delta, outside-keyed exact binding and
distinct consumed grant are prerequisites to any actual call.

The only operational strings are the three requested literal leaves:
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtinfo.so.6 and
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libkpathsea.so.6. The complete request, roles,
order and bounds are validated before any path operation. No target text,
request-reference path, directory member or decoded string becomes an
operand. The grant reference is typed DATA, not self-authenticating authority.

## Two different evidence types

A symlink receives lexical lstat/readlink(Buffer)/lstat only. All ten point
fields must match; returned byte length must equal the positive bounded
declared link size. Whole target bytes/hash are retained, plus reversible
UTF8 display when possible. There is no same-fd link identity, EOF/close
claim or target resolution. Non-UTF8 bytes remain exact hex, not normalized.
The primary [Node readlinkSync documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fsreadlinksyncpath-options)
supports returning link contents as a Buffer. The underlying
[readlink interface](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/readlink.2.html)
does not append a terminator; the complete link-size cross-check is explicit.
This is ordinary trusted API point evidence, not a hostile-race proof.

Each successful link is at most4096bytes, total12288. Node's whole-link API
does not expose a caller-set read buffer limit: if a concurrent size change
returns more, the entire actual returned Buffer is retained and the row
fails. No hard allocation/syscall/transport bound is claimed for that failure.
Negative/zero/oversize declared link size refuses before readlink. No magic
link fallback or second read is attempted.

A regular leaf follows the accepted same-fd algorithm: lstat, nofollow/
nonblock read-only open, full ten-field fstat comparison before bytes,
positive reads through actual zero EOF, after fstat/lstat, whole-size
agreement and successful close. All read counts, bytes, digest and close
errors remain. Bounds are16MiB/leaf and48MiB accepted total, plus at most
one failed overflow sentinel. The new failure row also hashes all retained
partial regular bytes; it does not label them complete. This is a new
explicit schema, not an unannounced mutation of the old reader/consumer.

Missing mandatory leaf, unsupported kind, changed key, read/open/close
error or exceeded bound stops at the first failed row. Available earlier
complete and current partial rows remain. A successful lexical link permits
continuing only to the other already listed primary leaves, never to that
link's target. After root receives the literal text, any terminal spelling
requires a separate exact selection. Neither a soname nor an apparently
familiar target proves identity with the accepted loader/tinfo bodies.
No suffix, automatic chain or fallback is selected here.

## Reuse and next gates

The ordinary bootstrap/Node/fs/crypto/product and trusted-ancestor boundary
is reused from the accepted S0 policy. No native14, statx, birthtime,
physical ancestor proof, continuous namespace or new observer-of-observer
layer is added. Earlier Bash/env startup stays explicitly limited.
The regular branch reuses the accepted control-flow argument, not an
operational import of the enabled eight-file entry. The new link branch
is the exact amendment needing independent source acceptance.

The serializer/exclusive separate stdout/stderr strategy may be reused,
but the old collect_files entry clamps an incompatible eight-file request.
A small exact new entry/binding/capture adaptation must be received before
any observation; ENTRY_REQUEST.proposed.json records that pending step,
not a runnable or already submitted command. Actual native/session return,
closed raw and new schema DATA reception remain necessary. Link-return
allocation failures or transport limits preserve failed/missing evidence;
no complete envelope is invented.

PACKAGE_SOURCE_REQUEST.proposed.json and PACKAGE_SOURCE_SCOPE.md request
only matching distributor/body/source-role evidence. They do not enlarge
this collector's three-leaf allowlist or authorize any package tool/query.
The32image/96state/64entry global gate stays; existing six decoded tables,
body pins,18init/fini entries and four cache candidates are reused, not
decoded again to count them. New kpathsea facts alone may justify one
later exact DATA interpretation and finite named follow-up, never recursion.

Actual preparation read the full next-step NOTE, full189-line accepted
reader and original S0 contract/policy receipt. Primary Node readlink and
selected loader source excerpts were consulted. No actual candidate/host/
private/proc lookup, readlink, observation, source import/test, grant,
science/build, child, central/Git operation or independent PASS occurred.

# Matching package/source roles — finite next DATA request

This is a request for evidence, not evidence that this host is Debian,
Ubuntu, RPM-based or any other distribution. No package/version/architecture
selection, download, package tool or local database query has occurred.
PACKAGE_SOURCE_REQUEST.proposed.json supplies the six exact accepted binary
pins and one intentionally unfilled kpathsea terminal role. Existing matched
receipts should be reused before requesting duplicate material.

First reuse the four exact existing DATA/ELF reception documents named in
the request. The only newly proposed local identity source is the literal
/etc/os-release leaf, separately scoped: accept only its actual complete
regular bytes or lexical link text, never shell-source it or automatically
follow to /usr/lib/os-release. It is NOT a fourth entry in this three-leaf
reader and requires separate exact source/selection authority. If an existing
authenticated distributor/build receipt already identifies these bytes,
reuse that receipt instead and omit this new identity observation.

The publisher/provider is then asked for at most seven MEMBER-SCOPED
records keyed by the listed original path and SHA256, followed by the exact
matching binary archive/member, signed index/checksum provenance, distributor
source/patches, build and debug/link-map records. Local package ownership
alone does not prove binary identity. A whole distributed member matching
the captured body, tied to authenticated package/build/source records, is
adequate ordinary provenance; no formally verified compiler or system
rebuild is imposed. Package member spelling may differ under usr-merge:
such a mapping must be explicit evidence, never an automatic host follow.

Exact URLs/package basenames are intentionally null until the distributor
and member record identify them. A source-only request must not invent an
Ubuntu/glibc/ncurses release from resemblance or fetch an arbitrary upstream
tag. Stop at HOLD_MATCHING_PACKAGE_RECORD_MISSING if no matching member
record exists. No entire /var/lib/dpkg/status, rpm database, apk inventory,
`dpkg -l`, filesystem walk, sibling glob or unnamed package search is proposed.
The next collection must pin the exact artifact names/URLs and selected
members before retrieval; unresolved names are not an executable request.

The concrete source-role targets are bounded:

- Bash: matching builtin exec role (candidate source member
  builtins/exec.def) and the already identified four init/fini origins.
- Env: matching main/environment assignment/exec and diagnostic/exit path
  (candidate member src/env.c), plus its four init/fini origins. Earlier
  inherited startup stays the accepted limit, not a new environment census.
- Kpsewhich/kpathsea: matching option/help/version/exit path (candidate
  member texk/kpathsea/kpsewhich.c), kpathsea_new and only the concrete
  helpers called before the selected exits; matched package records must
  identify their actual source members. Four existing kpsewhich origins
  and only subsequently received kpathsea origins require role mapping.
- Loader/libc: matching elf/dl-load.c, elf/dl-cache.c, elf/rtld.c,
  elf/dl-init.c, elf/dl-fini.c and relevant architecture/relocation/TLS
  support; generated trusted-dirs.h supplies the actual SYSTEM_DIRS rules.
  The [comparison loader source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bminor/glibc/glibc-2.35/elf/dl-load.c)
  explicitly consumes that generated header, but the comparison tag is NOT
  installed correspondence. Two existing libc array origins remain exact
  mapping targets; no whole-libc behavior proof is requested.
- Tinfo and shared CRT: match its four existing origins using package
  debug/link-map or bounded DATA relocation/symbol evidence. Matching
  libgcc/crtstuff.c routines may explain frame_dummy/dtor registration only
  if the received source/build/address evidence actually makes that mapping.

For every existing origin, retain image body pin, original descriptor/slot
span, relocation/symbol mapping, exact source member/span and its relevant
configuration/locale/load/child/exit branches. The already accepted18-origin
table is reused; no six-image redecode is needed. A concrete additional
resolver or helper is a named bounded branch, not permission to inventory
all possible constructors. ENV8 remains C.UTF-8/UTC. Cache OS/default cases
can be settled by applicable matched facts or a complete finite conservative
alternative set; customary directory names or guessed kernel/CPU facts are
not substitutes. All32/96/64 ceilings remain. No help/version/build gate is
opened by returning this request.
